verifications.claim: Southwest Airlines typically rebooks passengers automatically or offers a full refund to the original payment method if Southwest Airlines cancels a passenger's flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: In most cases, if Southwest cancels your flight, you will be automatically rebooked... refunds are processed to the original form of payment"; "you’ll receive a new itinerary automatically via email, text"
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states automatic rebooking and option for full refund to original payment when Southwest cancels.

verifications.claim: Passengers can manage, change, or cancel flights up to 10 minutes before departure via the Southwest website or app.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Most flights can be canceled directly on Southwest.com® or in the Southwest® app... You can cancel up to 10 minutes before"; "You can change your flight up until 10 minutes before your original scheduled departure time... through our website or the Southwest® app"
verifications.reasoning: Both R2 and R5 explicitly confirm changes/cancellations up to 10 minutes before via website/app.

verifications.claim: Southwest Airlines charges no cancellation fees for all fare types.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "No cancel fees. All fare types are eligible for cancellations without a fee."
verifications.reasoning: R1 repeatedly states no cancel fees for all fare types including Basic, Choice, etc.

verifications.claim: If a Southwest Airlines flight is canceled, passengers receive a notification via text or email with a new itinerary.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If Southwest texts or emails you with a new itinerary"; "you’ll receive a new itinerary automatically via email, text, phone call"
verifications.reasoning: Both sources confirm notification via text/email with new itinerary upon cancellation.

verifications.claim: If Southwest Airlines cancels a flight, passengers are entitled to a refund.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If your flight has been canceled and you decide not to travel, you are eligible for a refund"; "When you cancel your reservation, you will be presented with the option to receive a refund"
verifications.reasoning: Sources state eligibility for refund if airline cancels and passenger chooses not to travel.

verifications.claim: If a passenger cancels a flight, they generally receive a flight credit or Transferable Flight Credit™.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "your funds will be refunded as a Transferable Flight Credit™"; "you can receive a flight credit or Transferable Flight Credit™"; "you’ll receive a flight credit or Transferable Flight Credit"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm flight credit or Transferable Flight Credit upon passenger cancellation.

verifications.claim: Passengers must cancel at least 10 minutes prior to scheduled departure to avoid losing travel funds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Failure to cancel a reservation at least 10 minutes prior... may result in forfeited travel funds"; "You can cancel up to 10 minutes before... if you don’t... no-show policy will apply"
verifications.reasoning: Consistently stated across sources that canceling <10 min prior risks forfeiture/no-show.

verifications.claim: Southwest.com/rebook can be used to select new flights or request a refund.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "visit Southwest.com/rebook... to change your flight date and/or time... Option #4: Cancel your reservation and choose a method-of-payment refund"
verifications.reasoning: R4 specifies Southwest.com/rebook for rebooking new flights in cancellation context; refunds are an option when canceling via manage reservations.

verifications.claim: A significant flight delay is typically 3+ hours for domestic flights.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "typically 3+ hours for domestic flights"; "generally a delay of three or more hours domestically"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in both sources for domestic significant delay threshold.

verifications.claim: A significant flight delay is typically 6+ hours for international flights.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "typically 3+ hours for domestic flights or 6+ hours for international"; "six or more hours internationally"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in both sources for international significant delay threshold.

verifications.claim: If a flight is significantly delayed or canceled, passengers may be eligible for a refund even on non-refundable tickets.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "You are eligible for a refund if your flight is significantly delayed... or a flight cancellation"; non-refundable fares like Basic/Choice noted in R1 but exception here
verifications.reasoning: R3 confirms refund eligibility for significant delays/cancellations regardless of fare type.

verifications.claim: Passengers can change a flight to a new date within 14 days of the original travel date at no additional cost
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "you can change your flight date and/or time by up to 14 days from your original travel date at no additional cost"
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states this option in the context of airline cancellation, matching claim precisely.
